locator: I q.2 a.3 co., prima via: Certum est enim ... aliqua moveri in hoc mundo
interpretation: An existential premise taken as sense-evident (sensu constat), not demonstrated. It asserts only that some being is moved in some respect. Motus is read broadly: the article's own example is alteration (fire heating wood) and the stick-and-hand example is locomotion, so the respect is left abstract rather than restricted to locomotion. The formal premise is also compatible with the wider metaphysical reading of motus as any reduction from potency to act; choosing between the physical and metaphysical readings does not change this statement.
